candidate.blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — preoperative assessment and interpretation of diagnostic testing
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — individualized preoperative testing
candidate.educational_objective: Use individualized clinical indications rather than blanket panels when considering preoperative testing.

options.A: Use the same laboratory and diagnostic panel for every client regardless of health status or procedure.
options.B: Order tests even when the result would not affect perioperative planning.
options.C: Use test results instead of obtaining a preoperative history and clinical assessment.
options.D: Select tests according to the client's health, comorbidities, medications, ASA status, and type of surgery when the result could affect care.

candidate.rationale: Current NICE guidance does not recommend one universal preoperative test panel. Testing recommendations vary by surgery grade, ASA grade, comorbidities, medicines, and whether a result would influence management. D is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Routine preoperative testing is selected according to surgery grade, ASA grade, comorbidities, medicines, and clinical indication; many tests should not be offered routinely in low-risk situations.
candidate.source_document_title: Routine preoperative tests for elective surgery (NG45)
candidate.source_locator: Recommendations 1.2, 1.5-1.9; recommendations by surgery grade and ASA grade; Overview
candidate.source_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
candidate.stem: Which principle should guide routine preoperative testing for an adult having elective surgery?
